headline: Granted multiple variances, special permits, and continuances; cell tower hearing continued to February 25, 2026.
summary: The board acted on several zoning applications, granting variances and special permits for projects on South Terrace, Corning Street, Longview Drive, Bridge Street, Woodbury Drive, Cabot Street, and Federal Street. Several applications, including a proposed wireless communications tower at 12 Tozer Road, were continued to later meetings, and a few applications were withdrawn without prejudice.
decisions: Continued the application at 19 Dodge Street, Unit 110 to the February 25, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Continued the application at 21 Bridge Street to the February 25, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Granted withdrawal without prejudice of the 46 Federal Street LLC special permit, finding, and variance application, 4-0.
Continued the application at 12 Tozer Road (Verizon Wireless tower) to the February 25, 2026 meeting, subject to ample notification to abutters, 4-0.
Granted withdrawal without prejudice of the modification application at 371 Cabot Street, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 33 South Terrace to construct a 1,000 sq. ft. addition exceeding 25% of existing square footage, subject to Conservation Commission approval, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 33 South Terrace to construct an accessory dwelling unit in a nonconforming structure, subject to Conservation Commission approval, 4-0.
Found at 33 South Terrace that the front setback encroachment is not detrimental to the neighborhood, subject to Conservation Commission approval, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 100 Corning Street to construct a second-floor addition above an existing 1-story portion of the dwelling, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 21 Longview Drive to remove an existing garage and build a family room on the same footprint, 4-0.
Continued the application at 21 Beaver Pond Road to the February 26, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Granted withdrawal without prejudice of the application at 9-11 Fillmore Street, 4-0.
Granted a Parking Waiver at 297-299 Cabot Street due to proximity of public parking lots, 4-0.
Granted a Variance at 297-299 Cabot Street from Section 300-83A(2) due to narrow lot and building location, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 297-299 Cabot Street to convert a 2-unit structure to a 3-unit structure, 4-0.
Granted a Variance at 85-87 Bridge Street to separate and transfer a 1,175 sq. ft. parcel to the abutter at 93 Bridge Street, 4-0.
Granted a Variance at 11 Woodbury Drive for a single-story addition based on narrow lot and existing structure hardship, 4-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 11 Woodbury Drive as the proposed use will be in harmony with the neighborhood, 4-0.
Granted dimensional Variances at 46 Federal Street to build 5 new residential units, with a condition requiring 12-foot columnar arborvitae screening, 4-0.
plain_text:
CITY of BEVERLY 
Zoning Board of Appeals 
January 28, 2026at 6:00 pm 
  
These minutes are not a verbatim transcript of the public hearing of the Board of Appeals.  
Reviews of these Minutes or outcome of the public hearing should include an examination of the 
Board’s decision for that hearing.   
 
 
Members Present:  Will Cosmas, Chairperson, Cory Farinella, Laura Meisenhelter and  
   Benjamin Roy 
 
Others Present:      Jim Butler, Building Commissioner 
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant 
 
Location:        Council Chambers City Hall, 191 Cabot Street, Beverly 
 
 
Chairperson Will Cosmas began the meeting at 6:01pm, introduced the Board members present, 
and thanked the non-applicant attendees for taking part in the civic business of the City, 
particularly on a cold and snowy evening. 
  
 
CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
Keara Healy o/b/o Beverly Plaza LLC 
requests a Special Permit to propose a new set of channel letters at Russell Cellular/Verizon 
with a square footage of 46.71' which is greater than what is currently allowed by the Zoning 
Ordinance.  The property is located 19 Dodge Street, Unit 110 in the CG zoning district.  
 
The applicant submitted a written request to continue the application for 19 Dodge Street, Unit 
110 to the February 25, 2026, meeting. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to GRANT the request to continue the application at 19 
Dodge Street, Unit 110 to the February 25, 2026, meeting, subject to signing the Waiver 
and Agreement. Mr. Farinella seconded the motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Jason Irving/21 Bridge Street LLC 
request a Variance to subdivide the lot, retain the existing single family home and subdivide the 
existing lot to create a new second lot for the construction of an additional single family home.  
The addition of another single family home to the lot would be consistent with the general 
character and other lot sizes in the neighborhood.  The property is located at 21 Bridge Street in 
the R10 zoning district.
Page 2 of 18 
The applicant submitted a written request to continue the application at 21 Bridge Street to the 
February 25, 2026, meeting. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to GRANT the request to continue the application at 21 
Bridge Street to the February 25, 2026, meeting, subject to signing the Waiver and 
Agreement.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Alexander & Femino o/b/o 46 Federal Street LLC 
request a Special Permit, Finding and Variance to allow for the addition of 3 residential units 
to the existing single family residence which Beverly Historic Commission has found to be 
historically significant and preferably preserved.  In the alternative the single family can be 
demolished and replaced by 6 residential units by right.  The proposed requires a Variance for 
side and rear yard setbacks and a Special Permit and Finding for expansion of a legally pre-
existing nonconforming dwelling.  The property is located at 46 Federal Street in the RHD 
zoning district.   
 
Thomas Alexander, Esq. (Alexander & Femino) addressed the Board and stated that the applicant 
has decided to withdraw the application at 46 Federal Street without prejudice.  The applicant 
met with neighbors and has submitted a new application to be heard later this evening.  
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to GRANT the request at 46 Federal Street to 
withdraw the application without prejudice.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless and the Towers, LLC  
(To be heard no early than 7pm) 
requests a Special Permit under §§300-42 (C)(1)(p) and 300-91 height and setback Variances 
from §300-25A to permit a wireless communications facility with a monopole 124 feet in height 
(including 4' lightning rod) and setback from the property line of approximately 52'.  The 
property is located at 12 Tozer Road in the IR zoning district, Map 68, Parcel 25B.   
 
Michael Giaimo, Esq. (Robinson & Cole) addressed the Board and stated that the applicants have 
submitted additional materials.  On January 10, 2026, the applicants had a crane test conducted 
and held a community meeting.  A team took photos about a half mile at various locations around 
the site and produced a report including those photos.  Applicants have also submitted a report 
regarding the fall zone of the structure, a report on RF emission levels from different distances 
from the tower and generator specifications including sound data (64 decibels) at a distance of 23 
feet.  Atty. Giaimo stated that it is roughly the same sound emitted from a dishwasher for 
comparison and that noise dissipates from a distance.  The generator is tested every week for 15-
20 minutes. It won’t run continuously and the Board can specify a time that will have the least 
impact.  Applicants also submitted a property value report and an Affidavit from Chip Fredette, a 
site acquisition specialist for SAI Group, LLC, a company that works with Verizon Wireless,
Page 3 of 18 
summarizing his discussions with the City of Beverly in 2022 and 2023 which resulted in the 
RFP regarding the potential placement of a Verizon Wireless communications facility on Brimbal 
Hill water tower and his related interactions with the City through early April 2024. 
 
Atty. Giaimo read into record the Affidavit submitted by Chip Fredette.  
 
Atty. Giaimo reviewed the Photographic Simulation study of the crane test conducted on January 
10th, which according to the applicants placed an image of the proposed tower from the top point 
of the crane as seen from each location. 
 
Mark Correnti (Fairmarket Advisors), a certified appraiser, addressed the Board and provided an 
overview of the property valuation report that he prepared and the applicants submitted. 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked if there are any cell towers that Mr. Correnti reviewed but did not include in 
the report. Mr. Correnti stated when preparing a report, he looks for cell towers that are the same 
height. The report took a long time to develop because he had to research sales that met the 
criteria similar to the closest houses to this proposed cell tower. Mr. Correnti stated that therefore 
there were no cell towers that he reviewed but omitted from the report. 
 
Atty. Giaimo stated that the applicants meet both the state and local criteria for a Variance. The 
height of the tower needs to be tall enough to address the needs that Verizon is trying to alleviate.  
The minimum they can work with is 120’.  The site is a commercial area.  The trees aren’t 
perfect but they do help provide screening.  Atty. Giaimo stated that some courts in 
Massachusetts have held that the inability to fill a coverage capacity provides additional 
justification for a requested Variance.  
 
Keith Vallente, an RF Engineer (C-Squared Systems) speaking on behalf of the applicants, stated 
the height of the tower is a critical element of the structure, it has to be above any buildings, 
structures, trees, etc.  Mr. Vallante referred to the RF Report dated April 28, 2025 that was 
presented at the last meeting (Tab C). 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked if transmitters from other cell phone companies on the same tower would 
create interference.  Mr. Vallante stated there would not be interference from other co-locators as 
long as it is properly designed. Mr. Cosmas asked if Verizon plans to co-locate other antennas.  
Atty. Giaimo stated this tower would be built with that capability.  It is common practice.  
 
Ms. Meisenhelter asked Atty. Giaimo if there has been any response from the City as to why 
there was no response to the RFP a few years ago. Atty. Giaimo stated not to this knowledge. 
 
Kathleen Feldman (Ward 5) stated she fully supports her constituent’s opposition to this 
proposal. They are not denying the need for coverage in North Beverly. She feels they are here 
tonight because of a miscommunication.  It is the City’s desire for cell equipment to be installed 
on the existing water tower.
Page 4 of 18 
Cassie John, 9 Mark Road asked about the communications regarding the original water tower 
and if anything was sent by certified mail.  There is no proof with email.  Ms. John stated she 
believes that there is going to be 24-hour noise, not just from the generator running periodically 
but from whatever power source runs those at the base of the tower makes a lot of noise. It’s 
going to be 24 hours a day.  They are going to need cooling fans and that noise is going to travel. 
That droning hum goes right through you and you can’t be outside or open your windows. She is 
located two houses down from the tower and stated it is an eyesore.  The trees surrounding the 
site are old and they are falling. Once the tower is up there, its not going anywhere.  
 
Sherri McNeilly, 12 Walden Street, stated that she was affiliated with the Tozer Road 
Neighborhood Association and provided a petition with 57 signatures opposing the tower.  Ms. 
McNeilly would like to know what the distance of the closest house is to the tower. She believes 
its less than 200 feet. Ms. McNeilly asked what the hardship is that Verizon is relying on for this 
site.  
 
Thomas Winslow, 6 Mark Road stated he is concerned about the risk of the tower.  In the 
valuation report the comparisons showed towers in locations with very few houses, whereas this 
tower would be surrounded by 30 houses.  Mr. Winslow stated they need to minimize the risk. 
 
Marcus Bochman, 10 Walden Street stated he agrees that this is not happening at the water tower 
because of communication issues.  Also, even if the property values aren’t dropping, he 
personally wouldn’t have bought a house with this tower right in the backyard.  
 
Daniel Deangelis, 207 Brimbal Avenue stated he was not here at the last meeting because 
notification of an application of this magnitude is poorly done.  You can take a thousand pictures 
where you don’t see it but what matters is the 50 people who have signed the petition who will 
be able to see it.  He stated many people in the neighborhood were unaware that that crane was 
simulating a tower, they thought a tree was coming down.  Mr. Deangelis stated he thinks its 
disingenuous for the applicant to say that this crane is what the tower will look like, it is going to 
be much more than that. A slew of pictures was taken from Brimbal Avenue and it is just as 
prominent as it is on Mark Road.  Mr. Deangelis asked the Board to empathize with them as if 
this was going in their own backyard.  The fact that another option exists, this shouldn’t even be 
on the table.   
 
Walter Jankowski, 5 Mark Road stated he disagrees with the visibility photos, a lot of these 
pictures were taken strategically for Verizon.  
 
Arthur Boris, 9 Walden Street stated he opposes this tower.  The crane was put up at an angle, the 
trees aren’t covering all of it, it’s going to be a part of their neighborhood. 
 
Connie Macdonald, 7 Kinsman Street stated it’s a neighborhood that attracts families. Ms. 
MacDonald stated the photos shown of towers in other towns from Mr. Correnti’s report were 
shown in rural areas, not in densely populated neighborhoods.  She is also concerned that the 
tower will have lights on it. Ms. MacDonald is asking the Board to consider the quality of life of 
the residents and deny this request.
Page 5 of 18 
 
 
Alex, 1 Mark Road stated he is an abutter.  He asked if the owner of 12 Tozer Road is here. They 
were not present.  He is concerned with any glare coming from the tower.  The data shown this 
evening involved 4 homes. That is a weak number of homes to show for data, he would like to 
see that number around 25.  
 
Michael Dunn, 9 Mark Road stated if the water tower is an option, it is not necessary for his 
neighborhood to go through this.  
 
Beatrice Hines, 17 Conant Street stated all the other towers shown are up on a highway, an 
industrial park and commercial locations. No one has mentioned that these towers emit magnetic 
fields. They would be putting this right in the middle of a neighborhood where people live 24/7.  
Ms. Hines asked why it can’t go up at the city dump where the solar panels are if they can’t do 
the water tower.   
 
Fran Lucas, 10 Walden Street stated the photos that they showed with the tower was more in the 
country, there was grass and it was rural. Before the Board makes any decisions, they need to 
find out for sure what happened with putting it on the water tower.  Ms. Lucas stated she does 
not want this here.  
 
Atty. Giaimo requested to continue the application to the February meeting since only four board 
members were present.  Atty. Giaimo stated there are also questions that have been raised but 
can’t be answered tonight.  
 
Ms. Meisenhelter asked Atty. Giaimo if the intent is to go back to Verizon and question revisiting 
the water tower location.  Atty. Giaimo stated he thinks that they might be willing to do that with 
the comments made tonight. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to GRANT the request to continue the application at 12 
Tozer Road to the February 25, 2026 meeting, subject to ample notification to abutters 
and subject to signing the Waiver and Agreement.   
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
MODIFICATION REQUEST 
 
Original Request – August 2024: 
Alexander & Femino o/b/o Jesse Jalbert 
request a Special Permit/Finding under Sections 300-76B and 300-85A.1 of the Zoning 
Ordinance to change the present use allowed by special permit on the premises to 560 square feet 
of commercial space on the first floor and five (5) one bedroom units and one (1) two bedroom 
residential unit to be located on the first and second floors. The use, as modified, will be 
accomplished within the existing building footprint and envelope. The property is located at 371
Page 6 of 18 
Cabot Street in the CN zoning district.   
** Glovsky & Glovsky o/b/o Jesse Albert is requesting to amend Site Plan. 
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovksy & Glovsky) moved to withdraw the application at 371 Cabot Street 
without prejudice. 
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to GRANT the request to withdraw the 
Modification application at 371 Cabot Street, without prejudice.   
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
Brian Norris & Marcie Sidman 
request a Special Permit and a Finding to construct a 1,000 sq. ft. addition to be used as an 
ADU onto a nonconforming, single family dwelling exceeding 25% of the existing building 
volume.  The property is located at 33 South Terrace in the R10 zoning district. 
 
Bill Nolan (Savoie Nolan Architects) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicants and stated 
they are proposing to construct a new addition for an ADU. The house was built in 1931 with 
approximately 2,065 sq. ft. of living area. The front set back is nonconconforming and the only 
feasible place to construct the addition is out to the side. The applicants are proposing to build 
the ADU 6.2’ feet from the front property line, where the existing front setback is 3.5’. The 
addition will not be right on the street, it will be set 6.2’ back. There are two driveways on the lot 
and this is the only spot for the ADU.  The existing grade height to the first floor is of concern to 
the ADU occupant having to use exterior stairs.  There are a lot of mature trees on the property 
that the applicants want to maintain as part of this design. 
 
Mr. Nolan referred to the proposed ADU unit and indicated where most of the stairs were 
brought inside for safety.  It will be an open concept living room/kitchen area. It is an accessible 
space.  The square footage of the ADU is 1,000 sq. ft. in accordance with the Beverly ordinance 
and the existing house will remain the prominent structure.  
 
Mr. Nolan stated they need a Special Permit to allow an ADU in an R10 zoning district with an 
existing nonconformity.  They also need a Special Permit to expand an existing nonconforming 
dwelling more than 25%.  A Finding is needed to construct an addition in a front yard setback in 
the R10 district. 
 
Mr. Nolan submitted a letter in support of the application from the abutter at 54 South Terrace. 
 
Mr. Nolan stated they are also going through the Conservation Commission process.  There is 
conservation land near this property.  Mr. Cosmas stated that any ZBA approval is subject to the 
plans submitted so any changes required by the Conservation Commission will have to be 
resubmitted to the Board.
Page 7 of 18 
Mr. Roy stated it is a very unique neighborhood with lots of nonconformities.  Mr. Roy asked if 
they had any contact with the neighbor to the East. 
 
Marcie Sidman stated she feels very lucky to have such lovely neighbors.  Brian Norris stated 
that they are very happy to be able to do this and they have great supportive neighbors. 
 
Ms. Meisenhelter stated it’s a beautiful addition.  
No one spoke in favor or against. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to close the public hearing.   
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Farinella stated it’s a well thought out plan. Mr. Farinella asked for clarification as to the two 
Special Permits and Finding being requested. 
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 33 South Terrace to 
construct a 1,000 sq. ft. addition on a nonconforming single-story addition exceeding 
25% of the existing square footage, subject to plans submitted and approval of the 
Conservation Commission.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.  
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 33 South Terrace to 
construct an accessory dwelling unit in a nonconforming structure, subject to the plans 
submitted and approval of the Conservation Commission.   
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.  
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to Find at 33 South Terrace that the encroachment into 
the front set back is not detrimental to the neighborhood, subject to the plans submitted 
and approval of the Conservation Commission. Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Matthew and Jane Vaselkiv 
request a Special Permit/Finding to construct a second-floor addition above an existing 1-story 
portion of a lawful pre-existing nonconforming multi-family dwelling.  The property is located at 
100 Corning Street in the R10 zoning district. 
 
Matthew Vaselkiv addressed the Board and stated they are looking to construct a second-floor 
addition. It’s a legally nonconforming dwelling and they are staying within the building 
footprint. They are building a master bedroom and bath above the existing crawl space.
Page 8 of 18 
 
Mr. Vaselkiv provided two letters in support from abutters with the application. 
Mr. Cosmas asked for clarification that their address is unit 1 per City records.  Ms. Vaselkiv 
stated the home has two units; it is zoned as a multi-family. 
 
No one spoke in favor or against.  
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Ms. Meisenhelter asked for clarification that they are using the existing crawl space and Mr. 
Vaselkiv confirmed and stated they are using that and building above it. The previous owners 
added the addition off the back, but nothing above it.  
 
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 100 Corning Street to 
construct a second-floor addition above an existing 1-story portion of a lawful pre-
existing nonconforming multi-family dwelling, subject to the plans submitted.   
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.  
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Gary and Robyn Cole 
request a Special Permit to remove an existing garage and build a family room on the same 
footprint. The roofline will be 36” higher than existing garage roofline but will not exceed main 
house roof line. A front porch will be attached and meet setback requirements. A rear deck will 
also be added.  The property is located at 21 Longview Drive in the R10 zoning district.   
 
Gary and Robyn Cole addressed the Board and stated they are requesting a Special Permit to 
remove a nonconforming structure under 300-86C to construct a family room on the existing 
footprint.  Mr. Cole stated there would be no additional stress to the neighborhood, no trees being 
removed or views obstructed.   
 
Mr. Cole submitted 5 letters from abutters in favor of the project. 
 
Mr. Roy stated it looks straightforward. 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked what the increase of square footage is and Mr. Cole stated 336 sq. ft. 
 
No one spoke in favor or against.
Page 9 of 18 
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 21 Longview Drive 
to remove an existing garage and build a family room on the same footprint. The roofline 
will be 36” higher than existing garage roofline but will not exceed main house roof line, 
subject to the plans submitted.  Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
  
Glovksy & Glovsky o/b/o Roy L. Ruff, M.D. and Myra Ruff, Trustees of the  
Myra Ruff Trust and of the Roy L. Ruff Trust 
request a Variance to reduce side yard setback requirements from 20’ to 13.4’ and to increase 
maximum size from 100 sq. ft. to approximately 805 sq. ft. and maximum height from 10’ to 
approximately 20’, all to enable the construction of a detached 35’x23’ garage as depicted on 
plans filed with the application.  The property is located at 21 Beaver Pond Road in the R45 
zoning district.    
 
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) addressed the Board and stated the applicants are not 
here tonight, they are overseas.  The house is accessed by a private way.  It is a fairly remote area 
in the R45 zoning district.  They are looking to build an 800 sq. ft. detached garage 13.4’ from 
the setback.  This application is seeking relief for the size and height of the proposed garage due 
to it being in the side setback.  Atty. Walsh stated that there is a pool in the rear of the property 
and the lot is relatively narrow. There are also wetlands in both the front and rear of the property 
restricting where they can build.  
 
A letter from the abutters at 17 Beaver Pond Road in favor was submitted.  Attorney Walsh stated 
that it is the house most impacted by this project.  
 
Mr. Cosmas asked how this request is the minimum reasonable relief for a variance.  Atty. Walsh 
stated the square footage of the garage would be allowed by right but because they are requesting 
to build it in the side setback they require relief.    
 
Mr. Cosmas stated the photos in the application show an existing two car garage.  Atty. Walsh 
confirmed and stated they are being used for cars and storage.  Mr. Cosmas asked what the 
reason is for the 20’ height and Atty. Walsh stated it is the height that made sense to keep with 
the line of the house. 
 
No one spoke in favor or against. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.  
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the motion.
Page 10 of 18 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked for clarification as to what the applicants’ hardship would be to justify a 
variance, in part due to the pre-existing 2-car garage.  Atty. Walsh stated what exists is not 
adequate for their needs. The applicants feel they need additional storage on site.  Ms. 
Meisenhelter stated she is also struggling with the minimum relief being requested, although the 
wetlands on site to limit where they can build. 
 
Atty. Walsh requested to continue the application to the next meeting to discuss with the 
applicants.  
 
MOTION:   Ms. Meisenhelter moved to grant the request to continue the application at 
21 Beaver Pond Road to the February 26, 2026 meeting.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.   
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries. 
 
Alexander & Femino o/b/o John Jeremiah Vitale  
request a Variance to allow for an additional single family residence between 2 existing 
residences owned by the applicant.  The proposed lot (Parcel B-1) has 41.16’ of frontage, 5,133 
sq. ft. of area, would be set back 20’ from the front lot line, 7.1’ and 5.0’ from the side lot lines 
(which it shares with the applicant’s remaining land) and 25.0’ from the rear lot line.  The 2 
remaining lots would accommodate the existing 2 houses and would have frontage of 50’ and 
area of 5,000 sq. ft. for Lot 36(11Fillmore St) and frontage of 100.83’ and area of 9,064 sq. ft. for 
Lot A-1 (9 Fillmore Street).  Lot 36 (11 Fillmore Street) would have a new 13.3’ side yard 
setback.  Parcel A-1 (9 Fillmore Street) would have a new side yard setback of 15’ for the house 
and 45.5’ for the garage.  The present zoning for this district calls for 100’ of frontage.  10,000 
sq. ft. of area, side yard setbacks of 15’, front yard setback of 20’ and rear yard setback of 25’. 
The property is located at 9-11 Fillmore Street in the R10 zoning district.   
 
Thomas Alexander, Esq. (Alexander & Femino) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant 
and stated John Vitale has lived in the home for more than 20 years, and he is a veteran of the 
police force.  Last July there was an application submitted for this property and the proposed 
plans have been significantly redesigned to lessen the Variances required.  This property consists 
of two houses, with the addresses of 9 and 11 Fillmore Street. There is open space in between 
these two houses and that is where the proposed house lot would go.  This subdivision was 
created in 1912.  Many of the lots are 5,000 sq. ft. of area with 50’ of frontage based on the 1912 
subdivision plan.  The lot that the applicant owns were four lots on the 1912 subdivision plan.  
On Fillmore Street, seven of the houses are built to the 1912 subdivision plan dimensions.  This 
subdivision was largely built to accommodate modest housing.   
 
Atty. Alexander provided a comparison of what has changed between this application and the 
one in July.  Parcel B-1 is the new lot, Lot 36 is 11 Fillmore Street and Parcel A-1 is 9 Fillmore 
Street.  Mostly what has changed has to do with the new lot (B-1).  The lot area went down and 
is narrower, the front setback was 16’ in the prior proposal, it is now 20’ which eliminates the
Page 11 of 18 
need for a variance.  The lot conforms in the rear. The proposed deck in the back of the property 
has also been removed to decrease impact to the neighbor.    
 
Atty. Alexander reviewed the requirements for a Variance. The relief requested would not result 
in a detriment to the public good.  
 
Atty. Alexander provided a map showing which abutters have signed a petition in favor of the 
application. 
 
Mr. Cosmas asked if the application has a conflict with Section 300-78 of the Zoning Ordinance.  
Atty. Alexander provided a brief memo addressing this section of the ordinance and stated that it 
does not prevent the Board from granting a variance. Atty. Alexander also cited previous 
decisions by the Board that allowed the same or similar relief. Mr. Cosmas stated that the 
Board’s decisions are not precedential. 
 
Anita Walk, 13 Fillmore Street stated she has lived there for over 40 years, and this proposal 
doesn’t impose on anyone’s privacy.  It should be allowed; it’s another house that can be taxed 
and generate revenue for the City. 
 
Jim Chase, 4 Fillmore Street stated he has been there for 36 years, and he lives in one of the 
small 5,000 sq. ft. lots.  Mr. Chase stated he is in favor of the proposal. 
 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.  
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion. 
V otes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy) 
Motion carries.
